clauses.text:
Executive Order 10872
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE-  
TWEEN T H E  P A N  AMERICAN 
WORLD AIRWAYS, INC., A N D  
CERTAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Pan American World Airways, Inc.,  
a carrier, and certain of its employees  
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
way and Steamship Clerks, Freight Han­
dlers, Express and Station Employes, a  
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW,. THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pan American World Air­
ways, Inc., or by its employees, in the  
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (25 FR 2379, the issue of March 22, 1960) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10872, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated March 18, 1960. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by April 17, 1960), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 128 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 2, 1960; the board report states that the board was granted an extension of time to report to June 2, 1960. Thirty days after June 2, 1960 is July 2, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 2, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 2, 1960. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
